To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pre-edge peaks of the XANES spectra of titanium compounds increase with temperature.
the pre-edge peak intensity increases with increasing temperature, and that the AIIP can be used as a standard point for quantitative comparison of pre-edge intensities.
the temperature-dependent XANES spectra of Ti K-edge for ATiO3, A2TiO3, TiO2 rutiles and anatase can be used to quantify the intensity of the absorption features at the edge and the pre-edge region.

the temperature dependence of pre-edge peaks in the XANES spectra of Ti K-edge.
the temperature dependence of the pre-edge features of XANES spectra of titanium compounds.
the temperature dependence of the pre-edge features in XANES spectra of titanium compounds.

the pre-edge peaks of all compounds studied are due to transitions from the 1s state to 3d states.
pre-edge features in the Ti K-edge XAS of TiO2 rutiles and TiO2 titanates are temperature dependent and that this temperature dependence is a function of both temperature and chemical bonding.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temperature dependence of the pre-edge peak intensities in XANES spectra of Ti K-edges for ATiO3, A2TiO3 and TiO2 are mainly due to thermal vibration of the titanium atoms in TiO6 sites.
the pre-edge peak is a good indicator of the local structure of TiO6 octohedral sites.
the temperature dependence of the pre-edge features in XANES spectra is a good probe of the local structure around the absorbing atom.

temperature dependence of pre-edge peak intensity in XANES spectra of Ti K-edges can be quantitatively described in terms of thermal vibration of Ti atoms.
